title: Cognitive Dissonance Theory
text:
Cognitive dissonance refers to the mental stress or discomfort experienced by an individual who holds contradictory beliefs, values, or ideas, or is confronted by new information that conflicts with existing knowledge. Because this state of conflict is inherently uncomfortable, the drive is to reduce the discrepancy between cognitions.

The simplest methods for reducing this tension involve changing one of the conflicting behaviors or attitudes. Alternatively, individuals often minimize the importance of the dissonant beliefs or introduce new consonant beliefs that justify the conflict. For example, after making a major purchase, consumers frequently seek out confirming information about the product to reduce post-decision anxiety.
